result:
Unit 459 is finished, but criterion 9.4 is still open. The fldigi technique I took into our decoder improved the numbers overall, but it failed the keep rule (R78), so I reverted it. Everything is pushed to `main`, ending at `1f1c915d`, and `output.md` passes the report validator on all six rules.

**What the trace found (task 1).** In 18 places our decoder prints a letter as sure and gets it wrong while the port reads the same letter right (11 on real recordings, 7 on synthetic cases). The two biggest causes tied at 5 each: marks our decoder never picked up at all, and letters cut short by a gap rule or a speed that was too high. I chose fldigi's speed tracking because it is behind 6 of the 18, 5 of them real. The evidence: short noise bursts and dropouts push our window's speed estimate to 28ΓÇô40 WPM when the sender is at 17ΓÇô22. When I re-ran our own decoder on the same audio at the port's speed, it read four of those letters correctly.

**Result (task 2).** I wrote a synthetic test (exact key) copying the 032050 window: a sender at about 15 WPM with a 20 ms burst in every gap between letters and words. At the start it fails: 28 of 31 sure characters wrong. With the change in:
- **Real recordings:** sure-but-wrong characters fell from 33 of 436 to 25 of 431, invented characters from 33 to 25, coverage rose from 403 to 406, and word-boundary errors stayed at 37. The synthetic set didn't move.
- **Why it was refused:**
  - The adjudicated reading on 031948 broke: `110, AND 110ΓÇª` became `11Γûá AND 110ΓÇª`, so 12 of 13 adjudicated readings still pass.
  - Three recordings got worse. On 004507 `EACH` became `I ACH`, 031948 lost two right letters, and 032050's word-space errors went from 2 to 4.
  - Three more named floors fell below their marks.
- I reverted it in a separate commit. At exit every metric, floor and recording text matches the start of the unit. The fldigi port's output is byte-identical, `Cw/Second/` has no changes, and no source line differs over the unit.

**Things to know:**
- **The new test is still red in the tree** (`TheSpeedFollowsTheSendersMarkPairsTests`, 28 of 31 wrong). I left it failing on purpose as evidence for the open requirement. It isn't in either carry-forward line, so those stay green. If you don't want a failing test in the tree between units, that's your call.
- **I dropped task 3**, the named drop candidate. At the refusal I was 65 minutes in, past the unit's time window. Also, the trace shows the dahs on the 17:37 recording that task 3 would target are no louder than noise in our decoder's signal, so fldigi's detection method wouldn't recover them.
- **The instruction's list didn't match the tree twice.** The port also misreads 003758's first A, and it misses 004234's U, so neither counts. There is also no `.run-unit/watched.rc`.
- `.run-unit/watched.cpu` was modified again by the runner after my first commit and is left uncommitted. `SESSION.lock` belongs to the launcher, and I left it untouched.
